snippet.title: Even Coming Home Meant 30 Days of Waiting
snippet.description:
In 1377, Ragusa required arrivals from plague-affected places to wait 30 days before entering the city. The rule could apply to residents returning home, too. Later, a 40-day period gave us the word quarantine.

requested.title: Why Some Ragusa Residents Had to Wait 30 Days to Go Home
requested.description:
In 1377, the trading city of Ragusa—now Dubrovnik—required people arriving from plague-affected places to wait 30 days before entering. Even residents returning home could be made to wait.

The city was trying to reduce the risk of plague without shutting down the trade it depended on. A later 40-day waiting period gave us the word quarantine.
